lead.headline: Section of the Crimean Bridge collapses after a second night of Ukrainian strikes
lead.dek: Russia suspended road and rail traffic across the Kerch Strait; missiles hit two Kyiv bridges the same night
body: A section of the 19-kilometer Crimean Bridge collapsed overnight after Ukraine struck the road and rail link between Russia and occupied Crimea for a second straight day, and Russia's Transport Ministry confirmed Tuesday that traffic across the Kerch Strait is suspended, the Kyiv Independent and Al Jazeera reported. Video showed one steel arch and the roadway between two piers gone.

Ukraine's SBU security service said one arch and the automobile span beneath it were "completely destroyed." President Volodymyr Zelensky called the strike the seventh phase of a weeks-long operation that first took out air defenses, radars and electronic-warfare systems, crediting Neptune missiles, Palianytsia, Ruta and FP-5 drones and a Flamingo cruise missile. The ministry said preliminarily there were no casualties.

The Kremlin named Deputy Prime Minister Marat Khusnullin to lead a commission and opened a terrorism investigation; aviation expert Andrii Kharuk estimated the fallen section at 6,000 tonnes and a year or more to rebuild. The same night, Russian ballistic missiles hit Kyiv's Northern and Southern bridges over the Dnipro, which Mayor Vitali Klitschko said are closed; emergency services reported two deaths in Obolonskyi district.

briefs.headline: Stocks fall a third straight day as Nvidia slides ahead of its results
briefs.summary: The S&P 500 lost 1.92% and the Nasdaq 2.49% Monday; Nvidia fell 4.1% after a source told CNBC its board is not considering reinstating Jensen Huang, and Commerce moved to stop Chinese firms renting its chips through data centers abroad. Nvidia reports after the bell Tuesday.

briefs.headline: Trump lands in Manila for ASEAN ahead of Thursday's Xi-Putin summit
briefs.summary: He meets Quad leaders and signs a Thailand trade deal Tuesday, sees Marcos on Wednesday and flies to Shenzhen, where the White House says the first three-way meeting with Xi and Putin will focus on nuclear proliferation. Trump said he may also meet Kim Jong Un.

briefs.headline: Appeals court hears Trump's bid to move his hush-money case to federal court
briefs.summary: A three-judge 2nd Circuit panel heard more than an hour of argument Monday on intervening while New York's Appellate Division weighs his appeal of the 34-count conviction; one judge said he saw no procedural mechanism "authorized by Congress." No ruling was issued.

briefs.headline: Chase software bug knocks out online banking at several US banks
briefs.summary: Customers of JPMorgan Chase, Bank of America and U.S. Bank reported outages Monday, with nearly 4,800 Downdetector reports for Chase by 2 p.m. ET; Chase said a software bug, not a cyber issue, spilled into transactions with other banks, and service was normal by early Tuesday.

briefs.headline: Five EU states announce Rwanda deportation hubs opening by mid-2027
briefs.summary: Greece, Denmark, Germany, Austria and the Netherlands said Monday the first pilot return centers should operate by mid-2027; Euronews reported the first will hold about 100 people, citing people familiar with the talks.

briefs.headline: Houthis advance to within 60 km of Aden as Yemen's government pulls back
briefs.summary: Military and government sources told AFP the rebels took two Lahj districts after Yemen's government said Sunday it was redeploying forces from the Red Sea coast to defend Aden; the UN counts 1,600-plus dead since fighting resumed in July.

briefs.headline: South African police probe 17 killings in two weekend mass shootings
briefs.summary: Nine people were found shot dead Monday in a shack outside Pretoria and eight men in a vehicle outside Pietermaritzburg; Gauteng's police commissioner said the Pretoria deaths may be retaliation for a 2025 massacre, and no arrests have been made.

briefs.headline: Pope Leo ends his 12-day South America tour with a Lima Mass for 1.5 million
briefs.summary: The pope left Callao on Monday after a Mass at Las Palmas Air Base that the Vatican said drew about 1.5 million people, five weeks after lung cancer surgery; a thrown rosary appeared to strike his face in the popemobile beforehand.

briefs.headline: Federal grand jury indicts state Auditor Mark Hunt; he refuses to resign
briefs.summary: Hunt faces nine theft counts and aiding bank fraud over tax deeds his own Land Division staff had found ineligible, signed for an entity tied to a friend; four associates were also indicted. Speaker Hanshaw said the House will act in January if he stays; Morrisey called the allegations "troubling."

briefs.headline: Counties press PEIA to phase in a 24% Gold plan increase; Charleston hears it today
briefs.summary: At Monday's Shepherdstown hearing the WV Association of Counties said Gold High Deductible premiums have compounded nearly 66% since 2023 and asked for a two-year phase-in; the Finance Board hears Charleston on Tuesday and Wheeling on Thursday, with a December vote.

briefs.headline: Supreme Court lets the Hill Top House tourism-district law stand
briefs.summary: Justice William Wooton wrote for the majority rejecting five Harpers Ferry residents' challenge to the 2020 act, which exempts $25 million-plus projects in small towns from local zoning and building codes; Chief Justice Haley Bunn dissented on standing. The roughly $150 million hotel is the only project approved.

briefs.headline: Teamsters and The Beverage Market meet today on a pre-ratified contract
briefs.summary: Local 175's Luke Farley said the sides meet Tuesday on an offer the roughly 49 striking Charleston beer-distribution workers ratified last week, including a raise and a 60% rise in health premiums; the strike began May 12. The company did not respond to WVPB.

regional.item: The Cabell County Courthouse reopens on regular hours today after crews fixed an aging pipe on the county's side of the meter Monday; judges' offices will reschedule Monday's hearings.
Kanawha County commissioners certified the Nov. 3 election results at a special meeting Monday morning, and no candidate requested a recount.
The Wood County Solid Waste Authority told commissioners Monday it may lease about an acre of the former Fairplains School for a fenced, camera-monitored recycling drop-off.
Nicholas County deputies arrested a 47-year-old Glasgow man Friday night on a Kanawha County warrant in the Nov. 11 shooting of a man in the foot in Belle; bail is $50,000 cash.

away.item: Bennington's selectboard on Nov. 9 unanimously rejected rezoning 1033 Willow Road from rural conservation to rural residential and heard comment on alleged voter intimidation at the polls.

hotspots.item: Nelli, Webster County Schools' new vape and drug detection dog, debuted with her deputy handler at the Nov. 9 school board meeting, The Webster Echo reported Monday.
Pender school board members toured Topsail Middle on Nov. 12 to see a roughly $50 million plan for a ninth-grade Topsail High campus; the chair wants it under $31M.

briefs.headline: Prince George council puts off the CN Centre pause vote to Nov. 30, 6-3
briefs.summary: Coun. Cori Ramsay's motion to postpone the Klassen-Radloff-Steidle pause passed Monday with the three movers opposed; acting city manager Eric Depenau said staff will not proceed with the tender, due out Nov. 25, until they report back on contracts already approved and the cost of stopping.

briefs.headline: Quesnel asks the province to activate transition aid after the pulp mill curtailment
briefs.summary: The city formally requested Community Transition Services and opened talks with the Ministry of Jobs and Economic Growth after Millar Western indefinitely curtailed Quesnel River Pulp, the mayor said Monday; Millar Western is expected to detail supports for employees. Quesnel is about 120 km south of Prince George.

briefs.headline: Doerkson's Conservatives scrap a fall sitting; cabinet is sworn in Friday
briefs.summary: The incoming government said Monday it will not hold the shortened fall session it had floated, which would have run into December; Premier-designate Lorne Doerkson told CBC the legislative agenda begins in the spring sitting. No cabinet names were released.

briefs.headline: Kayaker's death is the fourth in four days on swollen rivers near Squamish
briefs.summary: A 29-year-old Squamish woman died Sunday after two kayakers flipped on the Cheakamus River, three days after a boat overturned on the Squamish River killing three, who are still unnamed; a 60-year-old man remains missing on the Fraser near Yale after a Friday capsize.
briefs.source: The Canadian Press via Yahoo News Canada

briefs.headline: Carney and Xi agree to drop China's 25% tariff on Canadian pork and shrimp
briefs.summary: At their Shenzhen meeting Tuesday morning China time, the leaders also opened China to Canadian fava beans, chickpeas and lentils, worth about $400 million a year in all, Carney's office said; Ottawa in turn extends tariff remissions to 32 more Chinese steel and aluminum items. Canola oil was not included.
briefs.source: The Canadian Press via Global News

briefs.headline: Canada's inflation holds at 3.1% in October as gasoline runs 30.9% higher
briefs.summary: Statistics Canada said Monday the CPI rose 3.1% from a year earlier, matching September, and 0.2% on the month; excluding energy it rose 2.0%, and groceries 2.0%. The Bank of Canada's December decision is "finely balanced," RBC's Abbey Xu said.

briefs.headline: West Antarctica's bedrock rebounds within decades, 3D mantle model shows
briefs.summary: A University of Colorado Boulder team reports in Science that ground under the Thwaites and Pine Island glaciers is rising up to 2 inches a year, because rapid ice loss sits over a weak upper mantle; the model spans 1900 to 2020.

briefs.headline: Webb finds water and carbon dioxide ice in Beta Pictoris' debris disk
briefs.summary: Astronomers report in Science the first direct detection of both ices around the 20-million-year-old star 64 light-years away; the water ice is overwhelmingly amorphous, with less than 7% crystalline, and about one CO2 molecule per 10 of water.

briefs.headline: At least 167 pregnant Americans have had measles since 2025, survey finds
briefs.summary: CIDRAP's canvass of state health departments found 101 of Pennsylvania's 1,561 cases this year in pregnant people; 11 departments did not answer and six states do not record pregnancy, so the count is a floor. One Pennsylvania mother and two newborns have died.

briefs.headline: Sentinel-6B passes its checks and takes over as the sea-level reference in January
briefs.summary: JPL said Monday the satellite launched a year ago was calibrated and cleared by Oct. 30; its twin, Sentinel-6 Michael Freilich, moves to a trailing orbit about 30 seconds behind so the pair can map the developing El Nino at higher resolution.

briefs.headline: Google says attackers automated an exploit chain with no human in the loop
briefs.summary: Google's Threat Intelligence Group reported Monday an exposed server running a framework that diffs patches, writes exploits and fires them, aimed at French sites; it counts zero-day exploits at 11 a month in 2026, against eight last year, with 22 in August.

briefs.headline: UNESCO-UCL study finds AI models cave on climate facts under pushback
briefs.summary: Of 15 models pressed to abandon correct answers, every one did, with accuracy falling 31 to 35 points; the 33 models tested scored 88 to 96% on basic facts but 33.8% on combined policy questions, about chance. The report goes to COP31.

briefs.headline: Harvard puts 403 hyperscale data centers at up to 1.8% of US electricity
briefs.summary: A Nature Sustainability study located the centers by satellite and estimated 68 to 99 terawatt-hours from May 2024 to April 2025, 54% of it from fossil fuels and 25.7 million tons of CO2, two to three times a 2018 estimate; it could not separate AI from other computing.

weather_ear: Jim Claudtore reads Tuesday's sky at 7:15.
kicker: Summers-New River carries no regional line for a 12th morning; PAHO briefs reporters today on the U.S. measles elimination status that CBS News and NBC News reported Monday has been revoked.
